newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia-Pacific pivotal to Compaq - executive.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific pivotal to Compaq - executive.

text.p: The Asia-Pacific operations of U.S.-based Compaq Computer Corp are pivotal to the future development of the company's global operations, a senior executive said on Thursday.
"The Asia-Pacific plays a pivotal role in the company's aim to be a top three global computer company," said Paul Chan, vice president and managing director of Compaq Computer Asia-Pacific.

Chan was speaking at a news conference after the Wednesday announcement of Compaq's global results in the U.S. showed profits surging 28 percent to US$1.3 billion and margins rising 24.4 percent for its 1996 business year.
"We were a significant contributor to that margin growth," Chan said. He declined to give an absolute figure.
He added he was "much happier today than a year ago in terms of our profitability".
But Chan said revenues from Compaq Asia-Pacific had "not made that much substantial progress" towards being 15 percent of global revenues by 2000, a target he set for the region last year.

He said they remained less than 10 percent of the total, although soaring sales have seen Compaq top league tables of market share revenues in Australia, Hong Kong, New Zealand, Singapore, China, Indonesia, Thailand and India.

Chan said Compaq was only sixth biggest in Taiwan and ninth biggest in Korea and despite impressive sales growth in those two countries of 60 and 70 percent respectively, only managed to maintain their market position.

He said "special plans" were being devised to correct this, but offered little detail, other than to say he hoped to gain leverage from the substantial local sourcing of materials Compaq makes in both countries.

Chan said pricing was still a major factor in sales in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly in countries like China and India, where he said he hoped to "hit the sweet spot in terms of pricing" with new mid-range ProLiant 5000 products.
